C-01.1.answer: Every new input refuses when absent: no answers file, an answer without a guard, a v2 file without a version, a finding without answer_failed under an answered class, a stopped class without a record, and a shell command that cannot be parsed are all refusals, never a pass.
C-01.1.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::absent inputs refuse: no answers, no guard, no version, no answer_failed, no stop-line record

C-01.2.answer: Each new rule has a control that deletes its input and expects red: removing the guard field, the revisions entry, the answer_failed field or the stop-line record turns the check red in the tests, so none of them is optional.
C-01.2.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::absent inputs refuse: no answers, no guard, no version, no answer_failed, no stop-line record

C-02.1.answer: The shell gate does not list writing commands to catch. It states the rule once: a command passes without answers only if every segment is provably read-only; anything else, including commands nobody listed, needs the answers for what the tree has changed.
C-02.1.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::the shell classifier: every read-only form passes and every writing form is caught

C-02.2.answer: The same rule (answer before any write to a tracked file) applies to every route: edit tools and shell in the hook, pre-commit for every staged file, CI per commit over the branch. The answers file rules (append-only, guards) are checked at commit and in CI, not only in the hook.
C-02.2.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::a shell command that may write is refused until the branch answers for what it changed

C-03.1.answer: Every new rule gets a test that runs it on the bad case first and sees it red for its own reason (the refusal text names the rule), then on the fixed case and sees it pass; the stop-line control checks the exact set of stopped classes in today's ledger.
C-03.1.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::control: the stop-line sees the classes stopped in the ledger, and only those

C-03.2.answer: The hook tests run the real findings-check script as a child process with a real hook payload and a real temporary git repository, so they observe the exit code and message Claude Code would see, not a stubbed function.
C-03.2.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::a shell command that may write is refused until the branch answers for what it changed

C-04.1.answer: The shell classifier reads at most 64 KiB of command text and refuses longer commands as unclassifiable; it splits once and does a constant amount of work per character, with no backtracking pattern. The bound is asserted by the refusal, not by a stopwatch.
C-04.1.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::a command longer than the bound is refused as unclassifiable, not parsed

C-05.1.answer: Every sentence added to docs/SELF_EVOLUTION.md and the spec names the test that checks it; the existing claims check still requires every backticked file name to exist. Ceilings (a waiver is self-declared, a guard proves existence not strength) are written as ceilings.
C-05.1.guard: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::each backticked file name in the docs appears in the code or the repository

C-05.2.answer: Each refusal prints what to do next: the answers file path, the missing question ids, the class that stopped and the record that would release it. A test acts on each message by doing exactly that and expects the next run to pass.
C-05.2.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::each refusal says what to do, and doing it passes

C-06.1.answer: Answers and waivers stay self-declared text and the docs say so. What changes is that an answer must point at a test that resolves, and a correction keeps the original, so a reader sees what was promised before the change and what proved it wrong.
C-06.1.guard: none: answers and waivers are the author's own words by design; the docs state that review judges their truth and that a resolving guard proves only that the test exists

C-09.1.answer: The hook is tested from a cwd outside the repository with absolute paths (a session started in a parent folder routes here), on a branch whose answers file is not yet committed, and on one where it is; git config and GIT_ variables are cleared in the child.
C-09.1.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::the hook works when the session started in a parent folder

C-10.1.answer: This change exists to turn rule text into gates: shell writes, rewritten answers, answers without a check, unrecorded misses and the stop-line review all move from documents into the hook, pre-commit and the CI range check, each with a test that fails when the gate is removed.
C-10.1.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::a class whose last two escapes upgraded nothing stops changes that must answer it

C-13.1.answer: The shell classifier is measured on both sides with one table: read-only commands it must pass (git status, grep, sed -n, npm test) and writing commands it must catch (redirects, tee, sed -i, cp, interpreters, heredocs, eval), including quoting and chaining.
C-13.1.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::the shell classifier: every read-only form passes and every writing form is caught

C-03.3.answer: The new checks fail on substance, not paperwork: a guard must resolve to a test that exists, a stopped class needs a detector the registry lists and that resolves (or a dated decision), and a miss under an answered question must name that question — a review file no longer releases anything.
C-03.3.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::every answer names a guard that resolves, or says none with a reason

C-09.2.answer: The Bash check finds its repository from its own file location, so it works when a parent folder routes the call; a test runs it with a cwd and payload from outside the repository. The parent routing itself was fed real payloads and denied a real edit while the answers were withheld.
C-09.2.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::the hook works when the session started in a parent folder

C-10.2.answer: Every route meets a gate: edit tools and shell commands in the hook, every staged file at commit, every commit in CI; the answers the gate read are frozen after the commit (append-only revisions), so changing them after the gate passed is refused rather than trusted.
C-10.2.guard: test/self-evolution.test.mjs::an answer, once committed, is never rewritten: corrections are revisions naming a finding
